q:
Match the concepts in column A with their respective descriptions in column B.

Column A
Column B

a. Gross national product
1. Annual income received by the individual’s production in a given period

b. Net national product
2. After the tax of personal income

c. Personal income
3. Money value of the national output

d. Disposable personal income
4. Net production of goods and services during the year
solution:
The correct answer is a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2.

Key Points

• The Gross National Product (GNP) is the money value of the national output.

• The Net National Product (NNP) refers to the net production of goods and services during the year after accounting for depreciation.

• Personal Income is defined as the annual income received by individuals from all sources.

• Disposable Personal Income is the income left after the deduction of personal taxes.

Additional Information

• Gross National Product (GNP)

• GNP measures the total economic output of a country, including earnings from foreign investments.

• It is an important indicator of a country's economic strength and performance.

• GNP includes the value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents, whether within the country or abroad.

• Net National Product (NNP)

• NNP is derived from GNP by subtracting depreciation of capital goods.

• It reflects the net output of the economy, accounting for the wear and tear on machinery and infrastructure.

• NNP is a key measure for understanding the sustainable economic growth of a country.

• Personal Income

• Personal Income includes wages, salaries, dividends, interest, rent, and any other income received by individuals.

• It is a broad measure of the income earned by residents of a country.

• Personal Income is used to assess the overall economic well-being of individuals in an economy.

• Disposable Personal Income

• Disposable Personal Income is the amount of money individuals have available to spend or save after taxes.

• It is a key indicator of consumer spending power and economic activity.

• This measure is important for understanding the financial health and consumption capacity of households.

q: Which of the following options is the most appropriate cause for unemployment in India?
solution:
The correct answer is Over population.

Key Points

• Overpopulation leads to a larger number of individuals competing for the same number of jobs, which increases the unemployment rate.

• With a high population growth rate, the number of job seekers increases faster than the number of available jobs.

• Overpopulation also puts a strain on resources and infrastructure, which can limit job creation and economic growth.

• In many cases, the education system and skill development programs cannot keep up with the growing population, leading to a mismatch of skills and available jobs.

Additional Information

• Unemployment

• Unemployment occurs when individuals who are capable of working and are actively seeking work remain un-hired. It is often used as a measure of the health of the economy.

• Types of unemployment include:

• Structural Unemployment: Caused by changes in the industrial makeup (structure) of the economy.

• Frictional Unemployment: Short-term unemployment that arises from the process of matching workers with jobs.

• Cyclical Unemployment: Resulting from economic downturns (recessions).

• Seasonal Unemployment: Occurs when industries slow or shut down for a season or make seasonal shifts in their production schedules.

• Overpopulation

• Overpopulation refers to a situation where the population exceeds the carrying capacity of the environment or the available resources.

• It results in environmental degradation, depletion of natural resources, and a higher level of competition for jobs, housing, and other services.

• Overpopulation can lead to higher levels of poverty and a lower quality of life for the population.

• Efforts to control overpopulation include family planning, education, and policies aimed at reducing birth rates.

• Economic Growth

• Economic growth refers to an increase in the production of goods and services in an economy over a period of time.

• It is often measured by the increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

• Economic growth can lead to higher employment levels, improved living standards, and an increase in the overall wealth of a country.

• Sustainable economic growth is essential for reducing unemployment and alleviating poverty.

q: Which of the following is an example of a non-tax revenue source for the government?
solution:
The correct answer is Fees and fines.

Key Points

• Non-tax revenue refers to the recurring income earned by the government from sources other than taxes.

• Fees and fines are common examples of non-tax revenue. Fees are payments made to the government for specific services or activities (e.g., passport fees, court fees), while fines are penalties imposed for violating laws or regulations.

• Non-tax revenue sources help the government fund its operations without increasing the tax burden on citizens.

• Other examples of non-tax revenue include interest receipts on loans given by the government, dividends from public sector enterprises, and income from government property.

Additional Information

• Personal income tax:

• It is a direct tax levied on the income of individuals.

• The rate of personal income tax varies based on income slabs and is progressive in nature, meaning higher income earners pay a higher percentage in taxes.

• Corporate income tax:

• This is a tax imposed on the net income or profit of corporations.

• It is a significant source of revenue for the government and is also a direct tax.

• Value-added tax (VAT):

• VAT is an indirect tax levied on the value added to goods and services at each stage of production or distribution.

• Consumers ultimately bear the cost of VAT as it is included in the purchase price of goods and services.

• Non-tax revenue sources:

• These include all government revenue sources that do not fall under the category of taxes.

• Examples include fees for services, fines and penalties, dividends from public enterprises, interest receipts, and revenue from government properties.

q: Which of the following is NOT the socio-economic objective of Industrial Policy Statement 1980?
options: Consumer protection against high prices and bad quality
Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment
solution:
The correct answer is Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment.

Key Points

• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 emphasized enhancing productivity, employment generation, and the optimum utilization of existing production capacity.

• It aimed at the promotion of export-oriented industries to improve foreign exchange earnings.

• The policy also focused on consumer protection against high prices and poor quality of goods.

• Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment (FDI) was not a primary objective of the Industrial Policy Statement of 1980.

Additional Information

• Industrial Policy Statement 1980

• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 was introduced to revitalize the Indian economy and make it more competitive.

• The policy emphasized modernization, technological upgradation, and the development of small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

• It aimed at achieving higher growth rates and industrial diversification to reduce regional disparities.

• The policy also sought to improve the efficiency of public sector enterprises and increase their contribution to the economy.

• Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)

• FDI involves investment from a foreign entity into the business interests of another country.

• It is a significant source of non-debt financial resources for the economic development of a country.

• FDI brings in capital, technology, and expertise, and can lead to job creation and infrastructure development.

• While FDI is important, it was not the main focus of the Industrial Policy of 1980, which was more oriented towards self-reliance and domestic industrial growth.

q: Which of the following statements is correct about the composition of the agriculture sector and employment in GDP post-independence?
options: The proportion of employment has declined significantly but not the share of the agriculture sector in GDP.
The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has increased significantly.
The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has declined significantly.
The proportion of GDP contributed by the agricultural sector declined significantly but not the employment depending on the agriculture sector.
solution:
The correct answer is The proportion of GDP contributed by the agricultural sector declined significantly but not the employment depending on the agriculture sector..

Key Points

• Post-independence, the share of agriculture in India's GDP has seen a significant decline. This is due to the growth of the industrial and service sectors.

• Despite the decline in the GDP contribution, a large proportion of the Indian workforce is still dependent on agriculture for their livelihood.

• Structural transformation in the economy is observed where the labor force shifts from agriculture to other sectors, but this transition has been slow in India.

• Employment in agriculture remains high due to slow industrialization and the inability of other sectors to absorb the growing workforce.

Additional Information

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP):

• GDP is the total monetary or market value of all the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.

• It serves as a comprehensive scorecard of a given country’s economic health.

• Agriculture Sector:

• This sector includes farming, fishing, and forestry, and it is a primary sector of the economy.

• It provides food, raw materials, and employment to a large section of the population.

• Employment in Agriculture:

• A large proportion of the workforce in developing countries like India is employed in agriculture.

• It includes jobs in crop production, animal husbandry, fisheries, and forestry.

• Structural Transformation:

• This refers to the shift of economic activities and labor force from agriculture to the industrial and service sectors.

• It is a key feature of economic development and involves changes in the structure of the economy.

q: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
solution:
The correct answer is Philips curve.

Key Points

• The Philips curve represents the inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.

• The concept was first introduced by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958.

• According to the Phillips curve, lower unemployment in an economy leads to higher wages, which in turn leads to higher inflation.

• This relationship suggests that policymakers face a trade-off between reducing unemployment and controlling inflation.

Additional Information

• Friedman's Model

• Also known as the Monetarist Theory, it was proposed by Milton Friedman.

• Friedman argued that there is no long-run trade-off between inflation and unemployment, as suggested by the Phillips curve.

• He introduced the concept of the Natural Rate of Unemployment, which posits that the economy will always revert to this natural rate despite short-term fluctuations.

• Friedman emphasized the role of monetary policy in controlling inflation.

• Keynesian Model

• Developed by John Maynard Keynes, this model emphasizes total spending in the economy (aggregate demand) and its effects on output and inflation.

• Keynesians advocate for active government intervention to manage economic cycles.

• They believe that insufficient demand can lead to prolonged periods of high unemployment.

• In contrast to the Phillips curve, Keynesians may support policies that increase aggregate demand to reduce unemployment without necessarily causing high inflation.

• Baumol Hypothesis

• Proposed by economist William J. Baumol, it addresses the cost disease in service sectors.

• Baumol's hypothesis suggests that wages in labor-intensive sectors (like services) rise due to wage increases in other sectors that experience higher productivity growth.

• This leads to higher costs in the service sector without corresponding increases in productivity.

• The hypothesis is often used to explain rising costs in sectors such as healthcare and education.

q: In which year was the MPLADS scheme implemented?
solution:
The correct answer is 1993.

Key Points

• Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) was launched in December 1993.

• The scheme enables Members of Parliament (MPs) to recommend developmental work in their constituencies with emphasis on creating durable community assets based on locally felt needs.

• Initially, the scheme allowed MPs to recommend works for Rs. 5 lakh per annum, which has now been increased to Rs. 5 crore per annum.

• The MPLADS funds can be used for various development activities including the construction of roads, schools, sanitation facilities, and drinking water facilities.

Additional Information

• Objective of MPLADS:

• The primary objective of MPLADS is to enable MPs to identify and fund small-scale developmental projects in their constituencies, addressing specific local needs and promoting the welfare of the people.

• Implementation:

• The MPLADS is implemented by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

• The funds released under MPLADS are non-lapsable, meaning they can be carried forward to subsequent years if not utilized within the financial year.

• Monitoring and Accountability:

• District authorities are responsible for the execution of projects recommended by MPs and ensuring that the funds are used appropriately.

• Regular audits and reviews are conducted to ensure transparency and accountability in the utilization of MPLADS funds.

• Recent Amendments:

• In recent years, the MPLADS guidelines have been amended to include provisions for funding projects related to COVID-19 relief and other national priorities.

q: In Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana, beneficiaries are provided with how much amount every year?
solution:
The correct answer is ₹6,000.

Key Points

• The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana (PM-Kisan) is a central sector scheme launched by the Government of India.

• Under this scheme, income support of ₹6,000 per year is provided to all farmer families across the country.

• This amount is paid in three equal installments of ₹2,000 each, which are directly transferred to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries.

• The scheme aims to support the financial needs of farmers in procuring various inputs to ensure proper crop health and appropriate yields.

Additional Information

• Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-Kisan)

• PM-Kisan is a central sector scheme with 100% funding from the Government of India.

• It was launched on 24th February 2019, and the first installment was paid out in December 2018.

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

• All landholding farmer families are eligible for this scheme, provided they meet the criteria set by the government.

• Objectives

• The main objective of PM-Kisan is to provide financial support to farmers, helping them to procure various inputs for agriculture and allied activities, as well as domestic needs.

• The scheme aims to supplement the financial needs of the farmers in procuring inputs for crop production, ensuring proper crop health and yields.

• It also aims to protect farmers from falling into the clutches of moneylenders for meeting such expenses and ensure their continuance in farming activities.

• Eligibility Criteria

• All landholding farmer families, which have cultivable landholding in their names, are eligible for this scheme.

• However, certain exclusions apply, such as institutional landholders, farmer families holding constitutional posts, serving or retired officers and employees of state/central government as well as public sector undertakings and government autonomous bodies, and professionals like doctors, engineers, and lawyers.

• Implementation

• The scheme is implemented through an electronic database containing the details of all the beneficiaries.

• The funds are directly transferred to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode.

• The states and union territories are responsible for identifying the farmer families which are eligible for support as per scheme guidelines.

q:
Which of the following statements about the aims of National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) of India is/are correct?

1. To make agriculture more productive.

2. To make agriculture more sustainable.

3. To promote organic farming.
solution:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

Key Points

• The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) aims to make agriculture more productive, sustainable, remunerative, and climate-resilient by promoting location-specific integrated/composite farming systems.

• It also focuses on improving soil health and water use efficiency, as well as enhancing seed quality and promoting the use of organic farming practices.

• The NMSA is designed to cover both rainfed and irrigated areas to ensure comprehensive coverage of all agricultural zones.

• It supports the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices that help in conserving natural resources while maintaining agricultural productivity.

Additional Information

• Soil Health Management (SHM)

• SHM is one of the major components of the NMSA. It aims to promote Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) through judicious use of chemical fertilizers, including secondary and micronutrients, in conjunction with organic manure and bio-fertilizers.

• The objective is to improve soil health and its productivity, thus supporting sustainable agriculture.

• Rainfed Area Development (RAD)

• RAD focuses on Integrated Farming Systems (IFS) for enhancing productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability.

• It includes crop diversification, horticulture, livestock, fishery, and agroforestry to make agriculture more resilient to climate change.

• Climate Change and Sustainable Agriculture: Monitoring, Modeling and Networking (CCSAMMN)

• This initiative aims to build and strengthen the capacity of farmers and other stakeholders in addressing climate change impacts on agriculture.

• It involves the development of climate-resilient agricultural practices and technologies, and promoting their adoption.

• Organic Farming

• The NMSA promotes organic farming through the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY). PKVY aims to support and encourage farmers to adopt organic farming practices and certifications.

• It also focuses on marketing organic produce to ensure better returns to farmers.

q: Under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, the maximum premium payable by the farmers will be  for all kharif food and oilseeds crops.
solution:
The correct answer is 0.02.

Key Points

• The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India.

• The maximum premium payable by the farmers is 2% for all kharif food and oilseeds crops.

• The scheme aims to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.

• It helps stabilize the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming.

Additional Information

• Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)

• The scheme was launched on 18th February 2016 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• It aims to provide a comprehensive insurance cover against the failure of crops, thus helping in stabilizing the income of farmers.

• Farmers are required to pay a uniform premium of only 2% for all Kharif crops and 1.5% for all Rabi crops. For annual commercial and horticultural crops, the premium is 5%.

• PMKSY was launched to improve farm productivity and ensure better utilization of the resources in the country.

• The scheme’s motto is "Har Khet Ko Pani" (Water for every field).

• It focuses on efficient water conveyance and precision water application devices like drips, sprinklers, pivots, rain-guns, etc.

• The scheme aims at improving on-farm water use efficiency through a proper combination of surface and ground water.

• The scheme aims at promoting soil test-based and balanced use of fertilizers to enable farmers to realize higher yields at lower cost.

• Under the scheme, farmers are provided with Soil Health Cards, which will carry crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilizers required for the individual farms.

• The Soil Health Cards will be issued once every three years for all land holdings in the country.

q: On 29th October 2020, the Ministry of Science and Technology launched the SERB-POWER Scheme. What is the objective of the scheme?
options: To allow reservation for women in the Parliament and Judiciary
To strengthen the solar programme of India with France
To mitigate gender disparity in science and engineering research funding in various academic programmes and laboratories
To allow reservation for women in the Ministry of Science and Technology
solution:
The correct answer is To mitigate gender disparity in science and engineering research funding in various academic programmes and laboratories.

Key Points

• The SERB-POWER (Promoting Opportunities for Women in Exploratory Research) Scheme was launched by the Ministry of Science and Technology on 29th October 2020.

• The primary objective of the scheme is to mitigate gender disparity in science and engineering research funding in various academic programs and laboratories.

• The scheme aims to empower women researchers by providing them with structured support in their research endeavors.

• It focuses on creating a conducive environment for women scientists to excel in their respective fields through grants, fellowships, and other supportive measures.

Additional Information

• Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)

• SERB is a statutory body under the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India.

• It was established through an Act of Parliament in 2008 and came into existence in 2009.

• The primary mandate of SERB is to promote basic research in emerging areas of science and engineering.

• The board supports research through various programs, grants, and fellowships.

• Gender Disparity in Science and Engineering

• Gender disparity in science and engineering refers to the underrepresentation of women in these fields.

• Several factors contribute to this disparity, including societal biases, lack of role models, and unequal access to resources and opportunities.

• Efforts to address gender disparity include providing scholarships, mentorship programs, and creating inclusive policies.

• Encouraging women's participation in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) is crucial for achieving gender equality and fostering innovation.

• Academic Programs and Laboratories

• Academic programs refer to structured courses and curricula offered by educational institutions to impart knowledge and skills.

• Laboratories are facilities equipped for scientific research, experiments, and measurement, providing hands-on experience and practical training.

• Both academic programs and laboratories play a vital role in advancing scientific knowledge and fostering research and development.

• Ensuring equal access and opportunities in these settings is essential for promoting diversity and inclusion in the scientific community.

q:
Identify the sequence of implementation of the following taxes.

I.Land revenue

II.Sales tax

III.MODVAT

IV.Service tax
solution:
The correct answer is I, II, III, IV.

Key Points

• Land revenue was one of the oldest forms of taxation implemented during ancient and medieval periods.

• Sales tax was introduced much later as a form of indirect tax on the sale of goods.

• MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax) was introduced in 1986 to allow manufacturers to obtain credit for the excise duty paid on inputs.

• Service tax was introduced in 1994 as a tax levied on services provided.

Additional Information

• Land Revenue

• Land revenue is a tax or revenue imposed by the government on the ownership or use of land.

• It has been a major source of revenue for many governments historically, especially in agrarian societies.

• In India, during the British rule, land revenue was a significant component of colonial administration.

• Land revenue systems like the Zamindari, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari were implemented in different regions.

• Sales Tax

• Sales tax is a tax levied by the government on the sale of goods and services.

• It is generally a percentage of the sale price and is added to the total cost paid by the consumer.

• This form of tax is an important source of revenue for state governments.

• With the introduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India in 2017, the sales tax regime was subsumed under GST.

• MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax)

• MODVAT was introduced in India in 1986.

• It allowed manufacturers to claim credit for the excise duty paid on inputs used in the production of goods.

• This system aimed to avoid the cascading effect of taxes and to make the tax structure more efficient.

• MODVAT was later replaced by CENVAT (Central Value Added Tax) and subsequently subsumed under GST.

• Service Tax

• Service tax was introduced in India in 1994.

• It was levied on specified services provided by service providers.

• Service tax was a part of the indirect tax regime and contributed significantly to the government’s revenue.

• With the advent of GST, service tax was abolished and integrated into the new tax structure.

Additional Information

• Global System of Trade Preferences (GSTP)

• It was established in 1988 during the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).

• It aims to promote trade among developing countries through the exchange of tariff concessions.

• India-Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Free Trade Agreement

• The GCC consists of Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.

• FTA negotiations started in 2004 to facilitate trade and economic cooperation between India and GCC countries.

• India-Republic of Korea Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)

• CEPA was signed in 2010 to foster trade and economic relations between India and South Korea.

• The agreement covers trade in goods, services, investment, and intellectual property rights.

• Trade Policy Review Mechanism (TPRM)

• It was established in 1989 under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and is now an integral part of the WTO.

• The 7th Trade Policy Review of India in 2021 aimed to evaluate and improve the transparency of India's trade policies.

q: If GNP is 16% higher than the last year and the rate of inflation is 9%, production in the economy has grown by:
solution:
The correct answer is 0.07.

Key Points

• The Gross National Product (GNP) is a broad measure of a nation's total economic activity.

• The GNP is 16% higher than the last year, indicating overall economic growth.

• Inflation rate is 9%, which represents the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services is rising.

• The production growth rate can be determined by adjusting the GNP growth rate for inflation.

Additional Information

• Gross National Product (GNP)

• GNP measures the market value of all the products and services produced in one year by labor and property supplied by the residents of a country.

• It includes the value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of the location of the actual production.

• Inflation

• Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services is rising and subsequently eroding purchasing power.

• Central banks attempt to limit inflation, and avoid deflation, in order to keep the economy running smoothly.

• Economic Growth

• Economic growth is an increase in the production of economic goods and services, compared from one period of time to another.

• It can be measured in nominal or real terms, the latter of which is adjusted for inflation.

• Calculation of Production Growth Rate

• To find the production growth rate, we adjust the GNP growth rate for inflation.

• Formula: Production Growth Rate = (1 + GNP Growth Rate) / (1 + Inflation Rate) - 1

• Using the given values: GNP Growth Rate = 16% or 0.16, Inflation Rate = 9% or 0.09

• Production Growth Rate = (1 + 0.16) / (1 + 0.09) - 1 = 1.16 / 1.09 - 1 = 1.0642 - 1 ≈ 0.07

q: What is subtracted from GDP to arrive at NDP?
solution:
The correct answer is Depreciation.

Key Points

• Depreciation refers to the reduction in the value of assets over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.

• In national accounting, GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measures the total economic output of a country.

• NDP (Net Domestic Product) is derived by subtracting the depreciation of the country's capital assets from its GDP.

• This adjustment is necessary to account for the loss in value of fixed capital and provides a more accurate measure of economic performance.

Additional Information

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP)

• GDP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given time period.

• It is used to gauge the economic performance of a country and make international comparisons.

• GDP can be calculated using three approaches: the production (or output or value added) approach, the income approach, and the expenditure approach.

• Net Domestic Product (NDP)

• NDP is calculated by subtracting depreciation from GDP.

• Depreciation, also known as the consumption of fixed capital, reflects the wear and tear or obsolescence of physical assets.

• NDP provides a clearer picture of the actual economic performance by accounting for the decrease in value of capital goods.

• Subsidies

• Subsidies are financial assistance provided by the government to individuals, businesses, or other entities to promote economic and social policy objectives.

• They can take various forms, including direct cash transfers, tax breaks, or price controls.

• Net Indirect Taxes

• Net Indirect Taxes are calculated as indirect taxes (like sales tax, VAT) minus subsidies.

• They are part of the factor cost adjustment to reach market prices in national accounting.

• Net Factor Income from Abroad

• Net Factor Income from Abroad is the difference between the income residents receive from abroad for factor services (like labor and capital) and the income paid to foreign residents for their factor services within the domestic economy.

• This measure is used to calculate Gross National Product (GNP) from GDP.

q: What was a significant negative environmental impact of the Green Revolution?
solution:
The correct answer is Soil degradation.

Key Points

• The Green Revolution led to the extensive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, which resulted in the degradation of soil quality.

• Overuse of these chemicals destroyed beneficial soil microorganisms, making the soil less fertile over time.

• High-yielding varieties of crops required more water and nutrients, leading to the depletion of soil nutrients and increased soil salinity.

• Monocropping practices associated with the Green Revolution reduced the organic matter in the soil, further contributing to soil degradation.

Additional Information

• Green Revolution

• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries, starting in the 1960s.

• Key components included the development of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of staple crops, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and the introduction of modern farming techniques.

• The main aim was to achieve food security and reduce hunger by increasing crop yields.

• Soil Degradation

• Soil degradation is the decline in soil quality caused by its improper use, usually for agricultural, industrial, or urban purposes.

• It involves the loss of soil's physical, chemical, and biological properties, which affects its ability to sustain plant life and provide ecosystem services.

• Factors contributing to soil degradation include erosion, salinization, compaction, loss of soil organic matter, and contamination by toxic substances.

• Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides

• Chemical fertilizers are substances that supply essential nutrients to plants in the form of compounds like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.

• Pesticides are chemicals used to kill or control pests that can damage crops.

• Excessive use of these chemicals can lead to environmental issues such as soil degradation, water pollution, and harm to non-target organisms.

• Monocropping

• Monocropping is the agricultural practice of growing the same crop on the same piece of land year after year.

• This practice can lead to soil nutrient depletion, increased vulnerability to pests and diseases, and reduced biodiversity.

• It often requires higher inputs of fertilizers and pesticides to maintain crop yields, contributing to soil degradation and environmental pollution.

q: When was the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana introduced to provide health insurance to people below the poverty line?
solution:
The correct answer is 2008.

Key Points

• The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) was launched by the Government of India in 2008.

• RSBY aims to provide health insurance coverage for Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.

• Under this scheme, beneficiaries are entitled to hospitalization coverage up to Rs. 30,000 for most of the diseases that require hospitalization.

• The scheme was designed to protect poor families from financial liabilities arising out of health shocks that involve hospitalization.

Additional Information

• Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY)

• RSBY was introduced by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.

• The scheme provides for cashless insurance for hospital services through an empaneled network of healthcare providers.

• Beneficiaries need to pay a registration fee of Rs. 30, and the government pays the premium to the insurer selected by the state government on the basis of a competitive bidding.

• The scheme covers all pre-existing conditions and there is no age limit for the beneficiaries.

• Transport expenses are also provided to the patient, within an overall limit of Rs. 1000.

• Health Insurance in India

• Health insurance in India is a type of insurance that covers medical expenses incurred by the insured due to health conditions.

• Health insurance policies can be purchased by individuals or families to cover a wide range of medical expenses, including hospitalization, surgery, and other medical treatments.

• Several government schemes like Ayushman Bharat, PM-JAY, and others aim to provide health insurance coverage to various segments of the population.

• The goal of these schemes is to reduce the financial burden of medical expenses and ensure access to quality healthcare services for all.

q: In which year did the Central Government launch the National Air Sports Policy?
solution:
The correct answer is 2022.

Key Points

• The National Air Sports Policy (NASP) was officially launched in the year 2022 by the Central Government of India.

• This policy aims to promote air sports in the country including activities like paragliding, hang gliding, ballooning, and aerobatics.

• The policy is designed to make India one of the top air sports nations by 2030.

Additional Information

• National Air Sports Policy (NASP)

• The NASP outlines the framework and guidelines for the development of air sports in India.

• It aims at ensuring the safety of participants, standardizing regulations, and promoting air sports activities.

• The policy encourages the establishment of air sports academies, training centers, and clubs to nurture talent and create job opportunities.

• The NASP also focuses on encouraging participation from all sections of society, including women and differently-abled individuals.

• Air Sports in India

• Air sports include activities like paragliding, skydiving, ballooning, aerobatics, and drone racing.

• These sports require high levels of skill, precision, and adherence to safety norms.

• India's diverse geography provides a natural advantage for a variety of air sports activities.

• The promotion of air sports can also boost tourism and create employment opportunities in the sector.

• International Context

• Countries like the USA, France, and Switzerland have well-established air sports ecosystems.

• By adopting international best practices and standards, India aims to elevate its status in the global air sports community.

• Collaboration with international air sports bodies will be crucial for the development of the sector.

q:
Consider the following statements and identify the INCORRECT statement(s).

1. The ‘Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0’ scheme has been implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2003.

Additional Information

• Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0

• This is a flagship program of the Government of India aimed at improving the nutritional and health status of children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.

• It is a Centrally-Sponsored Scheme and not under the National Food Security Act, 2003.

• Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)

• ICDS aims to provide food, preschool education, primary healthcare, immunization, health check-up, and referral services to children under 6 years of age and their mothers.

• The Act aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India's 1.2 billion people.

q: Which of the following institutions has contributed mainly in improving the economic status of the poor women in rural areas?
solution:
The correct answer is Self-help Group.

Key Points

• Self-help Groups (SHGs) are small informal associations of poor people, typically women, who come together to collectively save and lend among themselves.

• SHGs have been instrumental in empowering rural women economically and socially by promoting thrift, savings, and income-generating activities.

• They facilitate access to credit by linking with financial institutions, enabling members to start small businesses and improve their livelihoods.

• SHGs also play a significant role in fostering community development, enhancing social cohesion, and promoting gender equality in rural areas.

Additional Information

• Indira Awas Yojana

• The scheme aims to assist construction of houses for Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.

• It is now known as the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin).

• Integrated Development Project

• It is a development initiative aimed at the holistic development of various sectors such as agriculture, education, healthcare, etc.

• Rural Health Scheme

• This scheme is aimed at improving healthcare access and quality in rural areas.

• It addresses issues such as maternal and child health, nutrition, and communicable diseases.

q: Harrod Domar model was the main idea behind the  Five Year Plan.
solution:
The correct answer is First.

Key Points

• The Harrod-Domar model was the foundation for the First Five Year Plan of India.

• This plan was implemented between 1951 and 1956.

• The model emphasizes the importance of savings and investments for economic growth.

• It was aimed at addressing the country's immediate need for development in agriculture, irrigation, and energy.

Additional Information

• Harrod-Domar Model:

• This model is an economic growth model that was developed independently by Sir Roy Harrod in 1939 and Evsey Domar in 1946.

• The model suggests that the economy's growth rate depends on the level of savings and the productivity of capital investment.

• The key equation of the Harrod-Domar model is: Growth Rate = Savings Ratio / Capital-Output Ratio.

• The model highlights the need for investment to spur economic growth and the importance of efficient use of capital.

• First Five Year Plan of India:

• Launched in 1951, the First Five Year Plan focused on the primary sector, especially agriculture.

• It aimed to increase food production, improve irrigation facilities, and develop transport and communication infrastructure.

• The plan was successful in achieving its targets and laid the foundation for future economic planning in India.

• It also emphasized the need for industrialization to create job opportunities and improve the standard of living.

• Importance of Savings and Investments:

• Savings provide the funds necessary for investment, which in turn leads to economic growth.

• Higher savings rates can lead to higher investment rates, which can enhance productive capacity and increase GDP.

• Efficient allocation and use of savings are crucial for maximizing the returns on investment.

• Government policies often aim to encourage savings and investments through various incentives and reforms.

• Development Goals of the First Plan:

• To increase agricultural production to ensure food security for the population.

• To develop irrigation facilities to support agriculture and manage water resources effectively.

• To build infrastructure such as roads, railways, and ports to facilitate trade and movement of goods.

• To address the immediate needs of the country in terms of employment and poverty alleviation.

q: The Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP) for providing employment to people in drought prone areas was started by the Government of India during the .
solution:
The correct answer is Fourth Five-Year Plan.

Key Points

• The Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP) was launched by the Government of India during the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974).

• The primary objective of DPAP was to provide employment to people in drought-prone areas and to ensure economic development by stabilizing the income of the people living in these areas.

• The program aimed at reducing the adverse effects of drought on the productivity of land, water resources, and overall livelihood of the people.

• DPAP was part of the broader strategy of the Fourth Five-Year Plan to tackle regional disparities and promote balanced regional development in India.

Additional Information

• Five-Year Plans

• The Five-Year Plans of India were centralized and integrated national economic programs. The first plan was launched in 1951 and subsequent plans were formulated for five-year periods.

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) aimed at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.

• It focused on agriculture, including the Green Revolution, and improvements in industrial production.

• Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP)

• DPAP is one of the earliest area development programs initiated in India to address the issues of drought and desertification.

• The program focuses on the development of natural resources, including water conservation, afforestation, and soil conservation to reduce the impact of drought.

• It also aims to improve the socio-economic conditions of the people living in drought-prone areas through employment generation and infrastructure development.

• Regional Disparities

• Regional disparities refer to the differences in income, wealth, and living standards across different regions within a country.

• Addressing regional disparities is crucial for balanced and inclusive growth, ensuring that all regions benefit from economic development.

• Programs like DPAP are aimed at reducing these disparities by focusing on the development of less developed and drought-prone regions.

q: Money supply is a  concept.
solution:
The correct answer is stock.

Key Points

• Money supply is considered a stock concept because it represents the total amount of money available in an economy at a specific point in time.

• Unlike a flow concept, which is measured over a period of time, a stock concept is measured at one particular time.

• The money supply includes various components such as currency in circulation, demand deposits, and other liquid assets.

• Central banks and government agencies typically measure the money supply to monitor and manage the economy.

Additional Information

• Stock vs. Flow Concepts

• A stock concept is a quantity measured at a particular point in time. Examples include the money supply, wealth, and the number of goods in inventory.

• A flow concept is a quantity measured over a period of time. Examples include income, expenditure, and production.

• Components of Money Supply

• M1: This is the narrow measure of money supply, which includes currency in circulation and demand deposits (checking accounts).

• M2: This is a broader measure, which includes M1 plus savings accounts, small time deposits, and non-institutional money market funds.

• M3: This includes M2 plus large time deposits, institutional money market funds, and other larger liquid assets.

• Importance of Money Supply

• The money supply is a critical factor in determining inflation levels, interest rates, and overall economic stability.

• Central banks, such as the Federal Reserve or the Reserve Bank of India, use measures of the money supply to implement monetary policy.

• Changes in the money supply can affect the economy's performance, influencing everything from consumer spending to business investment.

q: What correctly defines change of inventories of a firm during a year?
options: Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the year
Production of the firm during the previous year – Sale of the firm during the year
Sale of the firm during the year – Production of the firm during the year
Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the previous year
solution:
The correct answer is Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the year.

Key Points

• Change in inventories refers to the difference between the production and the sale of goods in a given period.

• It helps in determining the amount of goods that are produced but not sold during the period.

• This metric is crucial for understanding the stock levels and inventory management of a firm.

• It impacts the working capital and liquidity position of the firm since unsold inventory ties up capital.

Additional Information

• Inventory:

• Inventory refers to the goods and materials that a business holds for the ultimate goal of resale.

• It includes raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished goods.

• Production:

• Production is the process of creating, expanding, manufacturing, or improving goods and services.

• It involves various stages of transformation of raw materials into finished products.

• Sales:

• Sales refer to the exchange of a good or service for money.

• It is the process of selling the produced goods to the end consumer or another business.

• Working Capital:

• Working capital is the difference between a company's current assets and current liabilities.

• It is a measure of a company's operational efficiency and short-term financial health.

Key Points

• The Green Revolution led to a significant increase in the production of food grains, but the growth was not uniform across all types of grains.

• While crops like wheat and rice saw substantial yield improvements due to the introduction of high-yielding varieties (HYVs), other grains like pulses and coarse cereals did not benefit as much.

q: In which five-year plan was the 'food, work, and productivity' slogan used?
solution:
The correct answer is Seventh.

Key Points

• The slogan 'food, work, and productivity' was used during the Seventh Five-Year Plan of India.

• This plan was implemented during the period from 1985 to 1990.

• The main focus was on increasing agricultural production, employment, and productivity in various sectors.

• It aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains and increase employment opportunities to reduce poverty.

Additional Information

• Five-Year Plans of India

• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs. These plans aimed at economic development and were formulated by the Planning Commission of India.

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture and energy.

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) aimed at the rapid industrialization of the country.

• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966) focused on agriculture and improving production of wheat.

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) aimed at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979) focused on poverty alleviation and achieving self-reliance.

• The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985) emphasized the elimination of poverty and technological self-reliance.

• The Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-1990) focused on "food, work, and productivity."

• The Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997) aimed at improving the quality of life, generating employment, and reducing inequality.

• The Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002) aimed at achieving a rapid and sustainable growth rate.

• The Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002-2007) focused on reducing poverty and achieving a growth rate of 8% per annum.

• The Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007-2012) aimed at inclusive growth.

• The Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-2017) focused on faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth.

• Planning Commission of India

• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.

• It was established in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Government of India, on the recommendation of the Planning Commission's Report.

• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) in 2015.

q: Ranjana Prakash Desai who became the first woman chairperson of the Press Council of India originally worked in which of the following organs of the government?
solution:
The correct answer is Judiciary.

Key Points

• Ranjana Prakash Desai is a former judge of the Supreme Court of India.

• She has served in the judiciary system and has made significant contributions to the legal field.

• As a judge, she has been involved in several landmark judgments and cases.

• Her appointment as the chairperson of the Press Council of India marks a significant milestone as she is the first woman to hold this position.

Additional Information

• Judiciary:

• The judiciary is one of the three pillars of democracy, the other two being the legislature and the executive.

• It is responsible for interpreting the laws, ensuring justice, and maintaining the rule of law in the country.

• The judiciary comprises various levels of courts, including the Supreme Court, High Courts, and lower courts.

• Judges in the judiciary system play a crucial role in adjudicating disputes, protecting rights, and upholding the Constitution.

• Press Council of India (PCI):

• The Press Council of India is a statutory body established under the Press Council Act of 1978.

• It aims to preserve the freedom of the press and maintain and improve the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.

• The PCI acts as a watchdog of the press, ensuring ethical standards and addressing complaints against the press.

• The chairperson of the PCI is typically a retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court.

• Supreme Court of India:

• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial authority in the country.

• It has the power of judicial review, which allows it to invalidate laws and executive actions that are inconsistent with the Constitution.

• It comprises the Chief Justice of India and a number of other judges as prescribed by law.

• The Supreme Court ensures the protection of fundamental rights and resolves disputes between the central and state governments.

q: Which state Chief Minister launched the 'Kaushalya Mattriva Yojana' in 2022, which provides financial assistance of ₹5,000 to women giving birth to a second girl child for safe motherhood?

Additional Information

• Kaushalya Mattriva Yojana:

• This scheme is specifically designed to provide financial support to mothers giving birth to a second girl child.

• The financial assistance aims to encourage families to value and support the birth of girl children, thereby addressing gender biases.

• It is part of a broader set of initiatives by the Chhattisgarh government to enhance maternal and child health.

q: Which of the following State governments has launched a scheme ‘Ankur’ in May 2021 to promote planting of trees in public, wherein people will be awarded for planting and taking care of the saplings?
solution:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

Key Points

• The Madhya Pradesh government launched the 'Ankur' scheme in May 2021.

• Environmental Importance of Tree Plantation

• Tree plantation plays a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance.

• Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, helping to combat climate change.

• They provide habitat and food for wildlife, thus preserving biodiversity.

• Trees prevent soil erosion and help in maintaining the water cycle.

• Government Initiatives for Environmental Conservation

• Green India Mission: Launched by the Indian government to protect, restore and enhance India’s diminishing forest cover.

• National Afforestation Programme: Aimed at increasing forest and tree cover to restore ecological balance and improve the quality of life.

• Namami Gange Programme: An integrated conservation mission to clean and protect the Ganga River by controlling pollution and rejuvenating its ecosystem.

• Community participation is essential for the success of environmental conservation efforts.

q: Which of the following is a component of the SHG-bank linkage program in India?
options: Microfinance institutions providing loans directly to SHGs
Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs
Non-governmental organisations providing capacity building training to SHGs
State government providing subsidies to SHGs for credit
solution:
The correct answer is Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs.

Key Points

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP) was launched by NABARD in 1992 as a pilot project to provide a cost-effective mechanism for providing financial services to the unreached and underserved rural poor.

• The program allows Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to open savings accounts in banks and avail loans.

• The SHG members collectively guarantee the repayment of loans, which reduces the risk for banks.

• This program has been instrumental in promoting financial inclusion and improving the socioeconomic conditions of rural women.

Additional Information

• Self-Help Groups (SHGs)

• SHGs are informal associations of people who come together to find ways to improve their living conditions.

• They are usually composed of 10-20 members who meet regularly to save and lend money to each other.

• The primary objective of SHGs is to promote savings and provide credit facilities to their members.

• SHGs play a crucial role in enhancing the socio-economic status of their members, especially women, by fostering a sense of community and collective responsibility.

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)

• NABARD is an apex development bank in India, established on 12 July 1982.

• It is responsible for providing and regulating credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village industries, handicrafts, and other rural crafts.

• NABARD also supports rural development projects by providing financial assistance and guidance.

• One of its significant initiatives is the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, which aims to link SHGs with banks to facilitate access to financial services.

• Financial Inclusion

• Financial inclusion refers to the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit where needed by vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups at an affordable cost.

• It aims to eliminate barriers to financial services and create opportunities for all individuals, especially the underprivileged, to participate in the formal financial system.

• Key components of financial inclusion include access to savings accounts, credit, insurance, remittances, and financial literacy.

• Promoting financial inclusion is crucial for achieving inclusive growth and reducing poverty.

q: _ is the provision of small credit to those who would have no other access to financial services.
solution:
The correct answer is Microfinance.

Key Points

• Microfinance refers to the provision of financial services to low-income individuals or those who do not have access to typical banking services.

• It includes a range of services such as microloans, savings, insurance, and money transfers.

• The primary aim of microfinance is to provide small loans to impoverished individuals to help them start or expand small businesses, thereby reducing poverty.

• Microfinance institutions (MFIs) play a critical role in providing these financial services, especially in developing countries.

Additional Information

• Microloan

• Microloans are small loans given to individuals who typically do not have access to traditional banking services.

• These loans are often used to start or grow small businesses and are a subset of microfinance services.

• Microloans can range from a few dollars to several thousand dollars, depending on the borrower's needs and the lender's policies.

• The concept of microloans was popularized by Nobel Laureate Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh.

• Homeloan

• A home loan, or mortgage, is a loan given by a bank or financial institution to individuals to purchase a home or property.

• Home loans are typically long-term loans with a repayment period ranging from 10 to 30 years.

• They require collateral, usually the property being purchased, to secure the loan.

• Interest rates on home loans can be fixed or variable, depending on the lender's policies and the borrower's agreement.

• Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)

• PMAY is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at providing affordable housing to the urban poor.

• The scheme was launched on June 25, 2015, with the goal of constructing 20 million affordable houses by March 31, 2022.

• It has two components: PMAY-U (Urban) for the urban poor and PMAY-G (Gramin) for the rural poor.

• Beneficiaries under this scheme are identified through the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) of 2011.

q: Which of the following is an example of joint sector industry?
solution:
The correct answer is Oil India Limited.

Key Points

• Oil India Limited is a joint sector industry in India, where both the government and private sector have stakes.

• It was formed under a partnership between the Government of India and Burmah Oil Company Limited, UK.

• The company is a Navratna company, indicating that it has been given financial and operational autonomy by the Government of India.

• Oil India Limited is primarily engaged in the exploration, development, and production of crude oil and natural gas, transportation of crude oil, and production of LPG.

Additional Information

• Joint Sector Industry:

• A joint sector industry is one where the government and the private sector collaborate in the ownership and management of the enterprise.

• The main objective of such an arrangement is to pool resources, expertise, and investments from both the public and private sectors to achieve economic development.

• These industries are characterized by shared ownership between the government (usually through public sector undertakings) and private companies or individuals.

• Examples of joint sector enterprises include Oil India Limited, which is a partnership between the Government of India and private stakeholders.

• Public Sector Enterprise:

• Public sector enterprises are organizations that are wholly or majority-owned by the government.

• Examples include Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) and Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

• Private Sector Enterprise:

• Private sector enterprises are businesses owned by private individuals or corporations.

• An example is Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), now known as Tata Steel.

• Navratna Companies:

• Navratna status is given to public sector enterprises in India that have comparative advantages, giving them greater autonomy in financial and operational decision-making.

• This status helps these companies to better compete in the global market.

• Oil India Limited is one such Navratna company.

q: What is the disinvestment target of the Finance Ministry for the year 2023-24?

The correct answer is ₹51,000 crore.

• The disinvestment target for the year 2023-24 set by the Finance Ministry of India is ₹51,000 crore.

• The aim of disinvestment is to reduce the fiscal burden and improve public finances by raising revenue from the sale of government assets.

• Disinvestment helps in achieving greater efficiency and competitiveness in public enterprises by involving private sector participation.

Additional Information

• Disinvestment:

• Disinvestment refers to the action of an organization or government selling or liquidating an asset or subsidiary.

• The primary objective of disinvestment is to reduce the financial burden on the government and to improve public sector efficiency.

• It also aims to increase the share of private sector investment in public sector enterprises and thereby improve their performance and competitiveness.

• In India, disinvestment is overseen by the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM).

• Fiscal Deficit:

• Fiscal deficit occurs when a government's total expenditures exceed the revenue that it generates, excluding money from borrowings.

• This deficit is an indication of the total borrowings needed by the government.

• Reducing the fiscal deficit is one of the reasons for government disinvestment, as it helps in managing public finances better.

• Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs):

• Public Sector Enterprises are government-owned corporations or state-owned enterprises created to undertake commercial activities on behalf of the government.

• They are often established to ensure the provision of public services and to promote economic development.

• Disinvestment in these enterprises is a way to involve private sector management and investment to improve efficiency and productivity.

• Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM):

• DIPAM is a department under the Ministry of Finance in India responsible for the management of government investments in equity and the disinvestment of government equity in public sector undertakings.

• It formulates policies and strategies for disinvestment in public sector enterprises to achieve the overall economic goals of the government.

q: Which of the following is Fisher's equation of exchange?
solution:
The correct answer is MV=PT.

Key Points

• Fisher's equation of exchange is represented as MV=PT.

• In this equation, M stands for the money supply in an economy.

• V represents the velocity of money, which is the rate at which money circulates in the economy.

• P is the price level, and T represents the total volume of transactions.

Additional Information

• Money Supply (M)

• The total amount of monetary assets available in an economy at a specific time.

• It includes various components such as currency in circulation and demand deposits.

• Changes in the money supply can influence inflation, interest rates, and economic growth.

• Velocity of Money (V)

• The rate at which money is exchanged from one transaction to another.

• It indicates the efficiency of money in an economy; a higher velocity means money is changing hands more frequently.

• Velocity is calculated as the ratio of nominal GDP to the money supply.

• Price Level (P)

• The average of current prices across the entire spectrum of goods and services produced in the economy.

• It is often measured by price indices such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) or the GDP deflator.

• Changes in the price level reflect inflation or deflation in the economy.

• Total Volume of Transactions (T)

• The total number of transactions or the total quantity of goods and services traded in the economy.

• This can include consumer spending, business investments, and government expenditures.

• The volume of transactions is an indicator of economic activity.

q: What was the main objective of the Second Green Revolution in India?
options: Ensuring food security in the western states
Focusing on holistic development in agriculture
Increasing the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides
solution:
The correct answer is Focusing on holistic development in agriculture.

Key Points

• The Second Green Revolution aimed at enhancing productivity sustainably through modern agricultural practices.

• It focused on diversification of crops, not just staple cereals, to ensure a balanced growth in agriculture.

• The initiative aimed to integrate technology and innovation in farming, including the use of biotechnology and precision farming.

• It also emphasized improving the income of farmers by promoting value addition, market linkages, and reducing the cost of cultivation.

Additional Information

• Green Revolution:

• The term "Green Revolution" refers to a series of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that took place between the 1940s and the late 1960s.

• It involved the development of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, increased use of fertilizers and irrigation methods, which significantly boosted agricultural production in many developing countries, including India.

• Biotechnology in Agriculture:

• Biotechnology refers to the use of living organisms or their systems to develop or make products. In agriculture, it includes genetic engineering, molecular markers, molecular diagnostics, vaccines, and tissue culture.

• It helps in developing crops that are resistant to pests and diseases, reducing the need for chemical pesticides, and enhancing the nutritional value of crops.

• Precision Farming:

• Precision farming is an agricultural management concept based on observing, measuring, and responding to inter and intra-field variability in crops.

• It involves the use of technologies like GPS, sensors, and data analytics to optimize field-level management with regard to crop farming.

• Value Addition in Agriculture:

• Value addition refers to the process of changing or transforming a product from its original state to a more valuable state.

• In agriculture, it involves processes such as cleaning, sorting, grading, processing, packaging, and branding which enhance the marketability and profitability of agricultural produce.

q: Which of the following movements created regional disparities between large and small farmers in India?
solution:
The correct answer is Green revolution.

Key Points

• The Green Revolution refers to the set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives occurring between the 1940s and the late 1960s that increased agricultural production worldwide, especially in developing countries.

• In India, the Green Revolution was launched in the 1960s with the introduction of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of seeds, increased use of fertilizers, and improved irrigation methods to boost food production.

• The Green Revolution led to a significant increase in food grain production, particularly wheat and rice, transforming India from a food-deficient country to one of the world's leading agricultural nations.

• However, the benefits of the Green Revolution were not evenly distributed, creating regional disparities and widening the gap between large and small farmers, as well as between different regions of the country.

Additional Information

• Yellow Revolution:

• The Yellow Revolution refers to the increase in the production of oilseeds in India, especially mustard and sunflower, initiated in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

• It aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in edible oil production to reduce dependence on imports.

• Pink Revolution:

• The Pink Revolution refers to the technological advancement and growth in the production of meat and poultry in India.

• It focuses on improving the quality and quantity of meat production, especially in the poultry sector.

• Blue Revolution:

• The Blue Revolution refers to the rapid increase in fish production and aquaculture in India.

• It aims to enhance the productivity of fisheries and aquaculture through sustainable practices and technological advancements.

Additional Information

• National Youth Policy

• The National Youth Policy (NYP) 2014 is an initiative by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.

• The policy aims to achieve a broad vision of empowering the youth of the country to achieve their full potential and to contribute to the development of the nation.

• The NYP 2014 outlines a comprehensive framework that covers the priority areas of education, employment and skill development, entrepreneurship, health and healthy lifestyle, sports, promotion of social values, community engagement, and youth participation.

• The policy also emphasizes the need for creating a productive workforce that can make a sustainable contribution to India's economic development and social well-being.

• Youth Empowerment

• Youth empowerment is a process where young people are encouraged to take charge of their lives and make informed decisions that affect their future.

• It involves providing opportunities for youth to develop their skills, gain access to resources, and participate in decision-making processes.

• Empowering the youth is essential for fostering innovation, economic growth, and social stability.

• Programs and policies aimed at youth empowerment focus on education, employment, leadership development, and community engagement.

• Skill Development

• Skill development refers to the process of improving the abilities and competencies of individuals to perform specific tasks or jobs.

• It is crucial for enhancing employability, productivity, and competitiveness in the job market.

• Governments and organizations implement various skill development programs to address skill gaps and meet the demands of the evolving labor market.

• Health and Healthy Lifestyle

q: Which of the following ministries launched the PM Daksh scheme?

Additional Information

• National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF)
